title: Publish the In-Service Teacher Professional Development Cohort Blueprint for Education Ministries, by Fri 11 Dec
description:
Education ministries, school districts, and teacher unions frequently run mandatory 4-to-6 week Continuous Professional Development (CPD) cohorts to train thousands of in-service teachers on modern pedagogy and digital skills. Traditional workshops fail due to poor post-event follow-through and fragmented WhatsApp groups. This blueprint equips educational agencies with a turnkey Zedu workspace architecture to deliver scalable, measurable teacher upskilling.

Work under this goal:
- Structure the multi-district CPD cohort workspace taxonomy: district-level subject channels (#district-math-cohort, #district-literacy), central ministry masterclasses, and peer coaching spaces.
- Author the weekly 45-minute peer lesson-plan critique protocol conducted via native Zedu Buzz live sessions.
- Standardize the weekly classroom evidence and micro-assignment submission thread workflow utilizing Zedu's 440px drawer for mentor grading rubrics.
- Build the master teaching resource and accredited curriculum distribution repository inside Zedu File Management with view-only teacher access.

Done when: A turnkey CPD operations package is delivered featuring district channel permission architectures, lesson critique run sheets, micro-credential submission templates, and verifiable ministry deployment steps.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Confirm Zedu's member and channel limits at ministry scale before promising "thousands of teachers"
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Ministry CPD cohorts can mean thousands of teachers at once. Approach: before writing the architecture, confirm with the team and the pricing page the limits that matter at that scale: members per workspace and per channel, call participants in Buzz, file storage per plan, and admin tools for bulk invites. Then size the design to fit: workspace per district or zone, channels per cluster of 30-50 teachers, facilitators as admins. Done: a limits table with sources and [CONFIRM] marks, the scaled structure, and the honest statement of what size the blueprint has been checked for.

upvotes.reason: "Confirm Zedu's member and channel limits at ministry scale before promising "thousands of teachers"" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

This is an important guardrail before marketing a ministry-scale use case: it checks workspace, channel, call, storage and bulk-invite limits before recommending a structure. The [CONFIRM] marks and stated tested scale prevent the blueprint from promising support the team has not verified.
Ministry-scale promises depend on member and channel limits nobody has confirmed. Checking them first stops the blueprint promising capacity the plan does not carry.
Checking member, channel and call limits before promising 'thousands of teachers' prevents an architecture the plan cannot carry.
A ministry buyer asks for member and channel ceilings first, and an untested limit claim is the fastest way to lose the deal. Confirming the real limits at that scale has to precede the blueprint.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Make CPD classroom evidence assessable and distinguish completion from accredited credit
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Build the CPD classroom-evidence submission workflow around teacher practice rather than pupil identities: offer an anonymized lesson-plan extract, a teacher reflection and an aggregate classroom observation as evidence routes; define what each can demonstrate and what a mentor cannot infer from it. Draft the weekly submission thread, a pre-upload redaction check, a mentor response rubric and an escalation route for accidentally identifying material. Use clearly labeled synthetic examples showing acceptable and unacceptable submissions, with no real learner records. Preserve assessment quality by connecting each route to the same stated weekly learning outcome; do not claim ministry accreditation or legal compliance. Done: one integrated evidence-and-feedback pack covering every selected weekly micro-assignment, approved by the CPD owner, with unknown product permissions explicitly blocked pending verification. Measure the share of sampled synthetic submissions that mentors can assess consistently and that pass the identifying-data check, reporting the sample and disagreements. Include an evidence-to-recognition table distinguishing participation, submitted work, assessed practice and programme completion from any professional credit requiring confirmation by the relevant authority. Supply proposed completion wording and three fictional pass/hold cases. Do not create another badge scheme, claim app-based attendance tracking or mint accreditation.
